explanation: An explicit constructor in C++ prevents implicit conversions, ensuring that object creation is intentional. When combined with default parameters, it allows for controlled and clear object instantiation, especially important in modern C++ to avoid unintended conversions and to improve code clarity. Explicit constructors are particularly useful in classes where implicit conversions could lead to bugs or ambiguous code, and default parameters provide flexibility in object initialization.
keywords: explicit constructor, constructor default arguments, constructor flexibility, prevent implicit conversion
